# pantechdynamics_certificate_export (Ephemeral Resource)

Exports a certificate with its private key, to install it outside Pantech, **without the key ever reaching the plan or state**. This is the recommended way to export (Terraform 1.10 and later); the pantechdynamics_certificate_export data source is for older Terraform and keeps the key in state. Use the values where ephemeral values are accepted, for example a write-only argument or a provider configuration. Only a certificate created with exportable = true can be exported, and only once it is issued, with an owner's or admin's API key that has the delete scope. **Every export is recorded and emails your organization's owners and admins a security notice**, so each Terraform run that exports sends one. A renewed certificate is exported again on the next run. An ephemeral resource is opened on every plan and apply that needs it, so each such run sends one email.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Recommended (Terraform 1.10 and later): export a certificate created with
# exportable = true without the private key ever reaching the plan or state.
# Use the values only where ephemeral values are accepted, such as a
# write-only argument or a provider block. Every export emails your owners
# and admins, so each run that opens this sends one email.
resource "pantechdynamics_certificate" "edge" {
  names      = ["edge.example.com"]
  exportable = true
}

ephemeral "pantechdynamics_certificate_export" "edge" {
  certificate_id = pantechdynamics_certificate.edge.id
}

# Then pass ephemeral.pantechdynamics_certificate_export.edge.private_key_pem
# and .full_chain_pem to a write-only argument (one whose name usually ends
# in _wo) of the resource that installs them, for example your secret store's
# provider, so the key is used during the run and kept nowhere by Terraform.
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `certificate_id` (String) Id of the certificate to export (cert_...).

### Read-Only

- `certificate_pem` (String) The certificate, PEM.
- `chain_pem` (String) The intermediate certificates, PEM, leaf excluded (may be empty for an imported certificate).
- `full_chain_pem` (String) certificate_pem followed by chain_pem, the form most web servers want.
- `id` (String) The certificate's id.
- `not_after` (String) End of validity of the exported certificate, in RFC 3339 UTC, to the second.
- `private_key_pem` (String, Sensitive) The private key, PEM (PKCS #8 for certificates Pantech issued). Sensitive, and never stored.
